To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adaptive inference is a promising avenue for future work in the design of MAB algorithms, and (2) doubly adaptive TS, a variant of TS that uses a doubly robust estimator to conduct inference on each arm, provides significant empirical benefits over existing baselines (TS, UCB).

(1) using an adaptive inference scheme in online decision making provides clear benefits in practice; (2) the benefits of adaptive inference are not at the expense of theoretical guarantees; and (3) doubly adaptive TS, which is a TS-style algorithm that uses adaptive inference, has superior practical performance to existing baselinesthough it has the same theoretical guarantees as UCB and TS.

(i) adaptive inference schemes can be used to unlock further performance gains in online decision making; and (ii) the proposed doubly adaptive TS algorithm is an effective and practical approach that achieves this.

, while worst-case regret guarantees are a useful tool for analyzing the performance of online learning algorithms, they are not a good predictor of the empirical performance of an algorithm in practical settings.
